title: Heavy-Duty Diesel Engine Exhaust Manifold Thermo-Mechanical Contact Analysis
source: Abaqus 2025 Example Problems - Thermal-Stress Analysis of an Exhaust Manifold; SAE Technical Papers on Heavy-Duty Exhaust System Durability
problem_description: Four-cylinder heavy-duty diesel engine exhaust manifold clamped to cylinder head via 8 high-strength preloaded bolts. The manifold experiences cyclical high-temperature exhaust gas (650 deg C) while the cylinder head is liquid-cooled (95 deg C). Analysis evaluates non-uniform temperature distribution, bolt preload retention, differential thermal expansion slip across the gasketed flange, and peak thermal stresses at runner junction fillets.

cylinder_head_block.material_name: Gray Cast Iron HT250 / A356-T6 Equivalent Cylinder Head Surface

loading_procedure.description: Steady-state convective heat transfer: exhaust runners internal convection (T_gas = 650 deg C, h = 320 W/m2-K); external ambient cooling (T_ambient = 50 deg C, h = 25 W/m2-K); cylinder head interface coolant conduction (T_head = 95 deg C). Generates spatial temperature field NT11.
loading_procedure.boundary: Prescribed coolant boundary temperature on cylinder head back-face

loading_procedure.description: Uniform cold bolt clamping: 8 bolts tensioned to 25.0 kN each (200.0 kN total clamping force) establishing initial normal contact pressure and seating the MLS gasket.

Lock bolt length (LOCK_LENGTH) and sequentially map the non-uniform temperature field NT11 from Step 0. Thermal expansion causes outward runner expansion, differential sliding (slip) against the cylinder head, and high thermal stress concentrations at runner junctions.

contact_interaction.interface: Manifold Flange to Cylinder Head via MLS Gasket
